card.title: Matrices and determinants: transpose, properties, inverse

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers of order m x n, and the special types that matter here are square, diagonal, identity, zero, symmetric (A = A^T) and skew-symmetric (A = -A^T, whose diagonal entries are all zero). The transpose interchanges rows and columns, (A^T)_ij = A_ji, with (AB)^T = B^T A^T, so the order reverses.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: x (AB)^T = A^T B^T. x (AB)^T = B^T A^T (order reverses!).  ·  x Every matrix has an inverse. x Only square, non-singular matrices.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A skew-symmetric matrix can also be symmetric only in the trivial case A = 0, since A = A^T = -A^T forces every entry to be zero.  ·  Interchanging any two rows, or any two columns, of a matrix changes the sign of its determinant.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Find the transpose and determinant of A = [[2,3],[1,4]].  ·  Find the inverse of A = [[1,2],[3,5]].

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: x AB = BA always. x Matrix multiplication is NOT commutative.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Find the transpose and the determinant of a 2x2 or 3x3 matrix, expanding a 3x3 determinant along the row or column with the most zeros.  ·  Find A^-1 for a 2x2 matrix by the adjoint method, then verify the result by multiplying A A^-1 to obtain the identity matrix.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Expand a 3x3 determinant along the row with the most zeros, which keeps the signs and the arithmetic simple.  ·  For a 2x2 matrix adj([[a,b],[c,d]]) = [[d,-b],[-c,a]], and A^-1 is that matrix divided by (ad - bc).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Find the transpose and the determinant of A = [[2,3],[1,4]].  ·  Find the inverse of A = [[1,2],[3,5]] and verify it by computing A A^-1.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Transpose questions are 1 to 2 marks and test the reversed order in (AB)^T rather than any computation.  ·  Finding a 2x2 inverse, or solving a 2x2 system by Cramer's rule, is a standard 5-mark question.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Order m x n means m rows and n columns; a matrix is square only when m = n.  ·  Transpose: (A^T)_ij = A_ji, so the order becomes n x m while the main diagonal is unchanged.  ·  The determinant of A = [[a,b],[c,d]] is ad - bc; it is a single number attached to the whole matrix, not to its entries.  ·  Singular matrix: |A| = 0, so no inverse exists. Non-singular: |A| != 0, so the inverse exists and is unique.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Matrix multiplication is not commutative, and (AB)^T = B^T A^T reverses the order for exactly the same reason.  ·  Only square matrices can have an inverse, and only when |A| != 0; a rectangular matrix has neither determinant nor inverse.  ·  The adjoint is the transpose of the cofactor matrix, not the cofactor matrix itself.  ·  |A^T| = |A|, and a 3x3 determinant uses the cofactor signs + - + along the first row.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Solve 2x + 3y = 8 and x - y = 1 by Cramer's rule.  ·  If |A| = 5 for a 3x3 matrix, find |adj A| and state the general formula for |adj A|.  ·  Show that A + A^T is always symmetric for any square matrix A.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Determinants of 3x3 matrices and the classification of matrices as symmetric or skew-symmetric are common 5-mark items.  ·  MCQs often ask which of the given matrices is singular, or ask for the order and entries after a transpose.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### 1. Matrix Definition  ·  A rectangular array of numbers arranged in rows and columns. Order: m x n (m rows, n columns).  ·  ### 2. Types of Matrices

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The adjoint adj(A) is the transpose of the cofactor matrix; A x adj(A) = |A| x I, hence A^-1 = (1/|A|) adj(A).  ·  Cramer's rule: x = Dx/D and y = Dy/D, where D = |A| and Dx, Dy are D with column 1 or column 2 replaced by the constants.  ·  For an n x n matrix, |adj A| = |A|^(n-1), so for a 3x3 matrix the power is 2.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Multiplying one whole row of an n x n matrix by k multiplies its determinant by k, not by k^n.  ·  The determinant of an odd-order skew-symmetric matrix is zero, even though the matrix itself need not be zero.  ·  If |A| = 5 for a 3x3 matrix then |adj A| = 5^2 = 25, not 5, because the exponent is n - 1.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The transpose interchanges rows and columns and satisfies (A^T)^T = A, (A + B)^T = A^T + B^T and (AB)^T = B^T A^T.  ·  For A = [[a,b],[c,d]] the determinant is |A| = ad - bc, and a matrix is singular exactly when |A| = 0.  ·  A^-1 = (1/|A|) adj(A) exists if and only if A is square and |A| != 0, and the inverse it produces is unique.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Cramer's rule solves ax + by = e and cx + dy = f by x = Dx/D and y = Dy/D with D = |A|.  ·  Determinants obey |AB| = |A| x |B| and |A^T| = |A|, while (A^-1)^T = (A^T)^-1 and A x A^-1 = I.  ·  Cramer's rule is only a substitution: copy D and swap column 1 for the constants to get Dx, and column 2 for Dy.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: If only |A| and |AB| are given, use |AB| = |A| x |B| and |A^T| = |A| instead of expanding anything.  ·  Solve using Cramer's rule: 2x + 3y = 8, x - y = 1.  ·  If |A| = 5, find |adj(A)| for a 3x3 matrix.
